definition: A training objective where random tokens in a sequence are hidden and the model learns to predict them from surrounding context.
details: Masked language modeling, used to train BERT, encourages bidirectional understanding of context, in contrast to the left-to-right prediction used by autoregressive models.
story: Imagine learning a language by reading every book in the library and noticing, over time, which words travel together. It does not memorize a rulebook; it absorbs a library. The machine learns language the way you did — by hearing so much of it that the patterns sink in. It is fluency built from pattern, not from memorized rules. And that is Masked Language Modeling — teaching a machine to read between the lines.

citation.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
